clue.text: Spots little son being given kisses

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son, as in genealogies
pecks are light quick kisses

explanation.surface: A small boy is being smothered in kisses by a doting relative.
explanation.definitionFit: Specks are tiny marks or dots, so they are spots in the sense of small blemishes.

clue.text: Bit of cash first pocketed by European

indicators.note: the abbreviation for first is held inside, pocketed by, the European

parts.note: a Pole is a native of Poland, a European
1ST is first, with the figure read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A coin first slipped into the pocket of a European.
explanation.definitionFit: This was an old gold coin of Spain and other countries, a piece of money.

clue.text: Bird caught landing on garden implement

indicators.note: in a down clue the letter sits on top of the implement

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a rake is a toothed garden tool

explanation.surface: A bird is caught as it lands on a rake in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A crake is a type of rail, a short-billed marsh bird such as the corncrake.

clue.text: Follower of team to drink beer

parts.note: to sup is to drink
porter is a dark, bitter beer

explanation.surface: A football fan going off to have a drink of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan who backs a club is one who follows the team, a synonym.

clue.text: Robert depressed about empty day, a severe setback

indicators.note: Robert's short form goes about, or around, the next piece

parts.note: Bob is the usual short form of the name Robert

indicators.note: an empty word keeps only its shell, the first and last letters of day

parts.note: feeling depressed means feeling low

explanation.surface: Robert is feeling down about a dull, empty day after a serious disappointment.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a punch to the torso, figuratively a heavy blow or major reverse in fortune.

clue.text: Laid into bed, judge gets tucked in

indicators.note: the word for judge is tucked inside the bed

parts.note: taken as the word bed itself
to rate is to judge or assess

explanation.surface: A judge is being tucked up in bed for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay into someone is to scold them harshly, which is what berating means.

clue.text: Article jamming pipe is an old coin

indicators.note: the article is jammed inside the pipe

parts.note: a duct is a pipe or channel
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Something stuck in a pipe turns out to be an antique coin.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a gold coin once used across European countries, now historical.

clue.text: Joyous socialist waffled

parts.note: blithe means happy and carefree
a red is a socialist or communist

explanation.surface: A cheerful left-winger rambled on and on.
explanation.definitionFit: To blither is to talk nonsense at length, so the past tense means rambled or prattled.

clue.text: Had too much on one's plate — but managed to deal with it!

definitions.text: Had too much on one's plate — but managed to deal with it!

parts.words: Had too much on one's plate — but managed to deal with it!
parts.note: the idiom for being overburdened is taken literally: someone faced a heaped plate and got through all the food

explanation.surface: Someone overloaded with work nonetheless coped.
explanation.definitionFit: Eating too much is literally having too much food on the plate and finishing it, a punning description.

clue.text: What pianist needs to get to manage black notes? Sly execution

definitions.text: What pianist needs to get to manage black notes?
definitions.meaning: the black keys play sharps, so a pianist must rehearse them: practice at sharps
underhand dealing, carrying something out deviously

explanation.surface: A pianist struggling with the black keys needs rehearsal; then a twist about something carried out slyly.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishonest or unscrupulous dealing for advantage is the idiom's everyday meaning, while the first reading puns on rehearsing sharps.

clue.text: First and second to enter wood

indicators.note: the short moment goes into, or enters, the wood

parts.note: a forest is a large wood
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: Someone is first in the woods, with a second person following them in.
explanation.definitionFit: Foremost means leading or most prominent, the one in front, synonymous with first.

clue.text: After short time what has managed to become country's biggest city

indicators.note: the rest of the pieces follow after the abbreviation for time

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
eh? is an exclamation meaning what?
ran is managed, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: Something that quickly grew into a nation's largest city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what' is not a pronoun here but the questioning exclamation EH; 'has' and 'to become' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran's capital is also by far its largest city, the country's biggest urban centre.

clue.text: Deficiency in desert

definitions.meaning: a flaw or shortcoming, as a noun
to abandon one's side for another, as a verb

explanation.surface: A shortfall found in a barren desert.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it means a fault or imperfection; as a verb it means abandoning one's country or cause.

clue.text: Overseas travellers will have this, going in a particular direction

definitions.text: Overseas travellers will have this, going in a particular direction

parts.words: Overseas travellers will have this, going in a particular direction
parts.note: people heading abroad toward the Orient are headed for, bound for, a particular compass point

explanation.surface: Travellers abroad all heading in one direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling toward the sunrise compass point describes heading in that particular direction.

clue.text: Modest daughter hugging lover finally expressed doubts

indicators.note: the modest daughter wraps round, or hugs, the next letter

parts.note: demure means modest and reserved

indicators.note: finally signals the last letter of lover

explanation.surface: A shy daughter cuddling her boyfriend eventually voiced some misgivings.
explanation.definitionFit: To demur is to raise objections or show reluctance, so the past tense means voiced hesitation.

clue.text: Storm is to put off drivers

indicators.note: put off in the sense of thrown off course, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A storm is set to deter people on the roads.
explanation.definitionFit: People who drive cars are drivers, so the word is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Upset about meal's last courses?

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: stressed means upset, anxious

explanation.surface: A diner is upset about the closing courses of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Puddings and sweets are served at the end of dinner, the final courses of the meal.

clue.text: English friend goes round old church that is historically significant

indicators.note: the friend encircles, goes round, the next two pieces

parts.note: a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: An English friend tours an ancient church of historic importance.
explanation.definitionFit: Something marking a new era, momentous, is of great importance in history.

clue.text: Using offensive words, tries to put off some going through snow?

definitions.text: Using offensive words, tries to put off
definitions.meaning: in cricket sledging is taunting a batsman to break their concentration
sleighs or ..., toboggans, are vehicles that cross snow

explanation.surface: Insulting someone to unsettle them, then a picture of vehicles crossing snow.
explanation.walkthrough: Sledging is cricket slang for fielders taunting a batsman to put them off their game.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means taunts to unsettle; as a plural noun it means snow vehicles, toboggans.

clue.text: I tried somehow to be less messy

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: Someone tried, one way or another, to be neater.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of tidy describes something neater, more orderly, with less clutter.

clue.text: Teams participating in chapel evensong

indicators.note: the answer takes part in, sits within, the words chapel evensong

explanation.surface: Sports teams are joining in with a chapel service.
explanation.definitionFit: Football and cricket sides have eleven players, so sides are commonly called this.

clue.text: Grab someone of distinction, competent but no leader

parts.note: a nob is a person of high social standing

indicators.note: the synonym loses its leading letter

parts.note: able means competent

explanation.surface: Seize a distinguished person who is capable, though not fit to lead.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to nobble someone is to get hold of or waylay them, to seize.

clue.text: One left in West Country city, not half one missing home?

indicators.note: the two letters sit in the shortened city
only half the city's name is kept, its first three letters

parts.note: Exeter is the county town of Devon in England's West Country
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A lone person left in a West Country city, half missing, perhaps homesick.
explanation.walkthrough: EXETER is the main city of Devon, in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone banished from their native land lives away from and longs for home.

clue.text: Tea before usual time? Bit of work about to be put into it

indicators.note: the turned unit goes inside the word for ahead of time

parts.note: early means before the usual time

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the unit is written backwards

parts.note: an erg is a small unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: Having tea ahead of schedule, with a bit of work to slot into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-known blend of black tea flavoured with bergamot oil, a type of tea.

clue.text: Good money abroad? Excellent!

parts.note: the rand is the currency of South Africa, foreign money

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled to get some good foreign cash.
explanation.definitionFit: As an exclamation it expresses delight, equivalent to great or splendid.

clue.text: Building complex redeveloped in e.g. south-east

indicators.note: redeveloped, as of rebuilt land, suggests the letters reorganised

explanation.surface: A building complex being redeveloped somewhere such as south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A planned area of homes built together is a residential development, a complex of buildings.

clue.text: Good boy, not completely thick, cheers up

parts.note: a lad is a boy

indicators.note: the synonym is not given in full, losing its final letter

parts.note: dense means thick, as of fog or of a dim person

explanation.surface: A well-behaved but rather dim boy brightens everyone's mood.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone happy is to cheer them up, the verb in the third person.

clue.text: Wicked person perched outside the underworld

indicators.note: the word for perched sits outside the underworld

parts.note: sat means perched
Dis is the Roman god of the underworld and its name

explanation.surface: A villain sitting just beyond the gates of hell.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who enjoys inflicting pain is a cruel, wicked individual.
